newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's BCN, BBA in acquisition talks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's BCN, BBA in acquisition talks.

text.p: Brazilian private bank BCN said it is in negotiations to sell a majority stake to Banco BBA Creditanstalt, but denied it had already sold such a stake to the bank.

In a statement sent to the Sao Paulo Stock Exchange (Bovespa), BCN said Banco BBA has showed interest in acquiring the control of BCN, adding that "studies and fact gathering, necessary in deals of that nature, have begun and are likely to last 30 to 40 days."
BCN said that "if these negotiations lead to an agreement which would be approved by the authorities, the market will be immediately informed."
With the statement in hand, Bovespa said it would resume trade in BCN stock on Friday.
Trade in BCN was suspended today following newspaper reports that the sale of the bank to Banco BBA was imminent and would be worth between $300 million and $500 million.
For months BCN and Banco BBA have been the subject of market speculation that a merger or acquisition deal would be announced any time soon.
Austria's Creditanstalt-Bankverein, which owns 49 percent of Banco BBA Creditanstalt, said it was looking into the deal, but had no concrete plans whatsoever yet.
Earlier this year BCN merged with local bank Banco Itamarati.
